summary: Add column, backfill, deploy a bidirectional sync trigger between note and customer_note, deploy new version, retire old, then drop old column after removing the trigger.
write_consistency: A PostgreSQL trigger mirrors writes between note and customer_note: on INSERT, both columns sync to the non-null value; on UPDATE, each changed column updates the other, ensuring both versions see the most recent write from either side.
revision_notes: Root cause: The drop_note_column SQL stage dropped the note column without first dropping the sync_user_note_trig trigger, causing a ProgrammingError when the trigger function referenced NEW.note on a column that no longer exists. Fix: added DROP TRIGGER sync_user_note_trig ON account_user; as the first SQL statement in the contract stage before dropping the note column.

stages.description: Add the new customer_note column to account_user.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;

stages.description: Copy existing note values into customer_note so the new version has data to work with.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE customer_note IS NULL;

stages.description: Create a trigger to keep note and customer_note synchronized during overlapping application versions.
sql: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_user_note_mirror() RETURNS trigger AS $$ BEGIN IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN NEW.note := COALESCE(NEW.note, NEW.customer_note); NEW.customer_note := COALESCE(NEW.note, NEW.customer_note); ELSIF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' THEN IF NEW.note IS DISTINCT FROM COALESCE(OLD.note, '') THEN NEW.customer_note := NEW.note; END IF; IF NEW.customer_note IS DISTINCT FROM COALESCE(OLD.customer_note, '') THEN NEW.note := NEW.customer_note; END IF; END IF; RETURN NEW; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER sync_user_note_trig BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_user_note_mirror();

stages.description: Deploy the new version (new-staged) with a state-only migration; the new Django model only knows customer_note.
Retire the old version (old) that still references the note column.
Remove the original note column now that the old version is gone.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
